analysis: Integration of four source passes. The PR adds .github/workflows/ci-dev-hourly.yml (head lines 1-38), a changelog fragment, docs in docs/developer/build.md (new row and 'Hourly full run of dev' section) and a guard test in scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py (HOURLY constant, classification at ~709-710, test at ~959-977). I verified the workflow directly from replayed head text. Triggers are schedule (cron '7 * * * *') and workflow_dispatch. Top-level permissions are {}. The single job on ubuntu-24.04 has only actions: write and contents: read. It has no checkout, no uses:, no secrets and no self-hosted or Darkbloom labels, so no PR-controlled code runs with the token. The only expression interpolations, github.token and github.repository, go through env vars rather than inline in the shell, so there is no script-injection vector. The API call and dispatch target only ci-dev.yml on dev. The workflow matches every assertion in the new test, including the exactly-one 'gh workflow run ci-dev.yml --repo "$REPOSITORY" --ref dev' command and the unfinished-run skip. The test tightens CI guardrails. Its classification means the existing no-self-hosted-labels checks cover the new workflow. No provider runtime, coordinator-provider protocol, attestation, App Attest, keys, prefix cache (T-041), fan helper or sandbox/GPU-limit boundaries (TB-002..TB-014; A-001..A-020) are touched, so the provider threat model is unaffected. Unverified contracts outside the evidence: dev's ci-dev.yml must accept workflow_dispatch and handle the 'Hourly full dev CI failures' issue with its own permissions. The docs state that a missing trigger fails with HTTP 422. Hourly full CI is a cost/availability matter, not a provider threat-model concern. Some replayed units were omitted (9 units), a coverage limit, but the changed files that matter were visible. No regression identified.
